recognize_zh: 許多紅血球內可見單一、圓形、深紫色、偏周邊的小顆粒（Howell-Jolly bodies），分布於不同細胞中，另見少數標靶細胞與棘狀紅血球，符合脾臟切除或功能性無脾的表現。
features: Numerous RBCs each containing a single small, round, dense dark-purple inclusion (Howell-Jolly body), usually eccentric
Inclusions are uniform in size (~1 um) and sharply defined, unlike the fine dispersed granules of basophilic stippling
Scattered target cells and occasional acanthocytes/irregularly contracted cells
A few RBCs with faint fine cytoplasmic stippling and slight polychromasia
Platelets present; no parasites or ring forms identified
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic red cells with mild anisopoikilocytosis. Numerous erythrocytes contain single, small, round, darkly basophilic inclusions consistent with Howell-Jolly bodies. Scattered target cells and occasional acanthocytes are present. No intraerythrocytic parasites are identified. Findings are consistent with Howell-Jolly bodies, suggestive of asplenia or hyposplenism.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are multiple, smaller, irregular granules clustered at the cell periphery and stain with Prussian blue, whereas Howell-Jolly bodies are single, larger, round DNA remnants.
Ring forms show a cytoplasmic ring with a chromatin dot, not a solid round dense body.
An overlying platelet is larger, granular, and often has a clear halo, whereas a Howell-Jolly body is a smooth, homogeneous, sharply defined dot within the cell.
